title: Fireline Handoff Sprintpad
content:
Shift: 22:00–06:00 
Owning engineer: Priya (you) -> handoff to Evan at 06:00
Purpose: compact, prioritized runbook + live status notes for tonight's overnight ops. Not a polished doc; use as quick reference and paste into ticket or pager when escalating.

1) Summary of last 6 hours
- Degraded autoscaler responsiveness 01:15–01:45: autoscaler controller issued multiple retry cycles due to transient GCE API throttling. Cleared by manual scale-up and temporary whitelisting in infra-proxy. See ENGOPS-423 for root cause analysis in progress.
- Minor Redis auth flaps on primary cluster at 03:02 — likely secondary key rotation conflict; failover succeeded, no data loss. Opened follow-up ticket (ENGOPS-423 -> subtask).
- No user-visible request latency SLO breaches after 02:10; steady token generation p50 110ms, p95 420ms as measured in prod-route /v1/generate.

2) Current live status (quick checks) — run these at handoff
- Kubernetes control plane: kubectl get nodes --no-headers | awk '{print $2, $3}' (expect Ready).
- Serving runtime queue depth: curl -s http://ops-api.internal/queues | jq '.generation.queue_depth' (should be < 200).
- GPU utilization (per pool): prometheus query: max_over_time(gpu_utilization_percentage[5m]) by (pool). If >90% for 10m, follow GPU overload steps.
- Redis primary role: redis-cli -h redis-primary info replication | grep role (should be role:master).
- Error budget burn rate: SLO dashboard -> last 1h burn < 5%.

3) If generation latency spikes (first-tier mitigation)
- Confirm spike across regions: Query CloudWatch/Datadog for p95 across components.
- Quick fixes (ordered):
  a. Bump dedicated pool instance count by +2 for affected model pool: kubectl scale deployment/model-pool-<name> --replicas=$(CURRENT+2).
  b. Toggle inference-batching to conservative: kubectl set env deployment/<runtime> BATCHER_MODE=conservative -n serving. Wait 45s and monitor queue depth.
  c. Enable fallback route to cheaper model variant: post to ops-api /routes/fallback with payload (model: <family>-small).
- If none work after 10 minutes, escalate to on-call SRE TL.

4) If KV cache miss storm (observed by rising recompute tokens)
- Check cache hit rate: Metrics -> kv_cache_hit_rate (should be >0.88).
- Temporary mitigations:
  a. Increase local cache TTL: curl -X POST http://ops-api/internal/configs/cache -d '{"kv_ttl":1800}' (Ops API auth required).
  b. Roll back recent config PR if merged within last 3 hours: git log --since='3 hours' --oneline infra/configs and revert.

5) If autoscaler is noisy (controller errors in logs)
- Quick patch: annotate deployment with autoscale-ignore=true for problem pool, then manually scale.
- Command: kubectl annotate deployment model-pool-<name> autoscale-ignore=true -n serving
- Notify infra-owner: Samir Patel (samir@redwood.ai).

6) Escalation contacts (in order)
- On-call SRE TL: Evan Morales — Slack @evan, mobile: +1-415-555-0179, email: evan.morales@redwood.ai
- Infra lead: Samir Patel — Slack @samir, email: samir@redwood.ai
- Product ops (if rollout/rollback needed): Jess Nguyen — Slack @jess, email: jess@redwood.ai
- CISO (if data exposure suspected): Marta Ruiz — email: marta@redwood.ai

7) Known issues and active work
- ENGOPS-423: autoscaler retries root cause — temporary fix applied 01:50; investigating long-tail API quota interactions. Owner: Priya.
- RED-512: redis auth rotation edge-case during multi-region failover. Containment: rotation paused for evening; follow-up planned for 2025-03-04. Owner: Samir.
- TODO: add more robust backoff in autoscaler (PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812).

8) Quickplay scripts and useful one-liners (copy/paste)
- Check serving pod logs (last 200 lines): kubectl logs deployment/runtime-serving -n serving --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
- Force a model pool scale-up (safe): kubectl scale --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy model-pool-bert -n serving -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}')+2)) deploy/model-pool-bert -n serving
- Rebind Redis primary (manual failover): redis-cli -h redis-sentinel sentinel failover mymaster
- Dump queue depth: curl -s http://ops-api.internal/queues | jq '.generation'

9) Misc / notes to incoming (Evan)
- Watch for any alerts tagged with "autoscaler" or "redis-rotation" in the first 30 minutes — those were noisy last night.
- If you need to perform a rollback of infra/configs, follow the rollback runbook in Confluence (link below) and ping me before midnight if possible.
- I left a partial log snapshot at /tmp/fireline-handoff-20250301.log (on jumpbox).

10) After-action checklist (for this shift)
- [ ] Verify ENGOPS-423 remediation steps are scheduled in roadmap.
- [ ] Create RCA draft for redis rotation (link to ticket).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler PR tests and green pipeline before merging next week.

References and links:
- Confluence runbook (autoscaler): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Autoscaler+Runbook
- ENGOPS-423: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENGOPS-423
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C1234/thread-ptl3
- PR for fix (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812

End notes: be pragmatic. If mitigation has user-facing impact, prefer quick rollback + targeted fix over multi-hour fiddling. Ping me (Priya) on Slack if you make any scaling or config changes with potential billing impact.

Signed-off: Priya Kapoor (on-call, night)
